account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended the program to rural areas with a machine-learning pipeline built with researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and Innovations for Poverty Action. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons, a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption, and the predictions determined who was paid. Beneficiaries registered themselves from their phones by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). NPR reported on 15 February 2021 that Eric Dossekpli, a farmer in Anfoin Avele, had received four payments and had used them for his children's school fees. In March 2022 the team that built the targeting published its evaluation in Nature. The authors found that phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives. In a hypothetical comparison with methods requiring a comprehensive social registry, which Togo did not have, phone-based targeting increased exclusion errors by 9–35%. In September 2023 the World Bank and the Government of Togo reported 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly with US$10 million. The same team ran a randomized trial of the first rural phase, published as a working paper in October 2023 and in the Journal of Development Economics in June 2025. The authors report that the transfers improved recipients' food security, mental health and self-perceived economic status. They also report that estimates of those effects from phone data do not match the survey results.

ai_role.statement: Decisive for who was paid: canton ranking and individual eligibility were both set by machine-learning predictions, while humans fixed the budget, thresholds and registration rules. The Nature evaluation is co-authored by the team that built the targeting method. The World Bank/Government of Togo case study is independent of the developers.

fields.account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended the program to rural areas with a machine-learning pipeline built with researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and Innovations for Poverty Action. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons, a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption, and the predictions determined who was paid. Beneficiaries registered themselves from their phones by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). NPR reported on 15 February 2021 that Eric Dossekpli, a farmer in Anfoin Avele, had received four payments and had used them for his children's school fees. In March 2022 the team that built the targeting published its evaluation in Nature. The authors found that phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives. In a hypothetical comparison with methods requiring a comprehensive social registry, which Togo did not have, phone-based targeting increased exclusion errors by 9–35%. In September 2023 the World Bank and the Government of Togo reported 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly with US$10 million. The same team ran a randomized trial of the first rural phase, published as a working paper in October 2023 and in the Journal of Development Economics in June 2025. The authors report that the transfers improved recipients' food security, mental health and self-perceived economic status. They also report that estimates of those effects from phone data do not match the survey results.
fields.summary: Machine-learning models using satellite imagery and phone metadata set eligibility for Togo's Novissi rural cash; 138,531 beneficiaries were paid from November 2020 to August 2021.

purpose: Prioritize the poorest cantons and the poorest mobile subscribers within them for COVID-19 emergency cash transfers in the absence of a social registry.

ratings.reason: Each of 138,531 rural beneficiaries received five mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men), according to Table 1 of the World Bank study. The developers' randomized trial reports gains in food security, mental health and self-perceived economic status. A beneficiary told NPR that he paid school fees with the money.
The Government of Togo delivered shock-responsive rural assistance without a social registry. The World Bank documents the model as a reusable case study.
The program reached 138,531 rural beneficiaries. The authors of the Nature evaluation report that exclusion errors were 4 to 21 percent lower than with geographic targeting.
